title: Studying PADI4 Polymorphism and Th17 cytokines profile in Rheumatoid Arthritis of Saudi Population
content: Peptidylarginine deiminase type 4 (PADI4) is involved in the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) by citrullination of proteins. PADI4 polymorphisms have been an issue of interest as they are related to RA, especially in Asian populations. Th17 cytokines have a pro-inflammatory role in RA. The vital Th17 cytokines involved are IL-17 A-F, IL-21, IL-22, and to a lesser extent IL-6 and TNF-α. This study was conducted to investigate the association of PAD4 polymorphisms with RA in the Saudi population. It also identifies Th17 cytokines profile (IL-6, IL-17, IL-22, IL-23, TGF-β, TNF-α, and TNF-RN) in Saudi RA for the first time. A total of 45 blood samples from Saudi participants (37 with RA and 8 healthy) were included 67% female while 33% were males. The extracted DNA from these samples was tested for rs11203366 and rs11203367 SNPs using the TaqMan SNPs Genotyping Assay by RT-PCR. Th17 cytokines levels were compared between healthy and RA patients. The two SNPs were significantly associated with RA in the Saudi population. Around 46% of RA subjects were homo allelic, 64% were hetero allelic while all healthy subjects were found to be hetero allelic. The study found that IL-6, IL-17, IL-22, and TNF-α were at higher levels in Saudi RA patients, TGF-β at lower levels, while IL-23 and TNF-RN did not significantly change compared to healthy subjects.
